results.title: GPU Rental Prices Are Rising Again: What the October 2026 Nebius and AWS Changes Mean for Inference Cost
highlights:
After falling in 2025, H100 rental prices rose in 2026. Nebius raised list prices on 1 October and AWS raised Capacity Blocks on 7 October. Here is what the numbers show and how to plan for them.

...

In short

- GPU rental prices fell in 2025 and are rising in 2026. Nebius raised its H100 on-demand price from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour on 1 October 2026.
- AWS raised EC2 Capacity Blocks prices by about 15% in October. AWS on-demand prices did not change.
- One price index put the median on-demand H100 SXM at $4.20 per GPU-hour on 7 October 2026. Hyperscalers charged a median of $10.53 for the same GPU.
- The "price per GPU-hour" you see is a list price. Your real cost per token depends on utilization, and a half-idle GPU costs twice as much per token.
- Plan for price drift: use commitments for steady load, keep workloads portable, and track cost per token, not cost per hour.

...

Key point

Two large providers raised GPU prices within a week of each other, reversing the 2025 trend.

The Uvik GPU Price Index (captured 7 October 2026) lists the dated events. On 1 October, Nebius raised H100 on-demand from $3.85 to $4.50 (+17%). It raised H200 from $4.50 to $5.40 (+20%). On 7 October, AWS raised EC2 Capacity Blocks prices by about 15%.

The Nebius pricing page I fetched today matches the new numbers. It lists H100 at $4.50, H200 at $5.40, B200 at $8.50 and B300 at $9.50 per GPU-hour. It also says prices may change at any time.

IntuitionLabs checked AWS on 10 October 2026. The Capacity Blocks rate for P5 (H100) is $5.970 per GPU. In July 2026 it was $5.191 in US regions and $4.720 in other regions. By my calculation from those figures, that is about +15% in the US and about +26.5% elsewhere. AWS says the rates are next scheduled to be updated in January 2027.

Note

Capacity Blocks are reservations, not on-demand. IntuitionLabs warns against using them for cross-provider comparison. AWS on-demand prices did not change in this round.

The earlier trend matters too. AWS cut on-demand prices by 44% for P5 (H100) in June 2025. Then the SemiAnalysis one-year H100 contract index rose from $1.70 to $2.35 per GPU-hour between October 2025 and March 2026. That is +38%. IntuitionLabs attributes a roughly 40% contract rise to HBM3e cost pass-throughs from Samsung and SK Hynix. That is the article's explanation, not a statement from the providers.

...

The Uvik index covers 19 providers and 87 public on-demand prices. It excludes spot, marketplace, reserved and contract-only prices. For the H100 SXM it found a median of $4.20, a low of $3.20 (Hyperstack and Thunder Compute) and a high of $12.29 (Microsoft Azure).

Split by type, the four hyperscalers had a median of $10.53. The 12 GPU clouds had a median of $3.95. That is a 2.7x gap. Across all GPUs in the index the hyperscaler multiple runs from 1.7x to 2.7x.

...

Commitments change the picture. Uvik says three-year commitments cut H100 prices by 56% to 57% at AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure. That narrows the hyperscaler gap, but only if you can predict three years of demand.

...

- After falling in 2025, GPU rental prices rose in 2026: on 1 October 2026 Nebius raised H100 on-demand from $3.85 to $4.50 (+17%) and H200 from $4.50 to $5.40; AWS raised EC2 Capacity Blocks by about 15% (a reservation product, not on-demand, which did not change; next update scheduled January 2027).
- The Uvik index (19 providers, 87 public on-demand prices) put the median H100 SXM at $4.20 per GPU-hour on 7 October, with a hyperscaler median of $10.53 versus $3.95 for 12 GPU clouds (2.7x). Three-year commitments cut H100 prices by 56% to 57% at the big three.
- Which provider you rent from matters more than the month you rent in.

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing in 2026: Are Prices Falling? | FastGPU
highlights:
Over 46 days to September 15, 2026, we tracked the cheapest on-demand price for every major GPU across 28 clouds, and the surprise was what did not happen: prices did not fall. In that study window the cheapest guaranteed H100 bounced between roughly $0.99 and $1.75 an hour with no sustained direction, and the newest Blackwell cards, rather than sliding as supply arrived, settled onto a flat plateau. What has not stalled is the gap between that floor and what the big clouds still charge for the identical chip. As of November 14, 2026, the same H100 rents from $1.73 an hour on the cheapest provider, while the cheapest hyperscaler on-demand rate is $5.38 ( Google Cloud) and Oracle lists it at $10.00 per GPU-hour, 5.8x the floor. When the study closed, Azure's own published on-demand rate worked out to about $12.29 per GPU-hour - Microsoft Azure Retail Prices API. The story of GPU pricing in 2026 is not a fall. It is a market that found its floor while the penalty for renting from the wrong place stays enormous.

...

Make that concrete with the H100 as it stands today (November 14, 2026). On spot, the cheapest interruptible rate is $0.82. On guaranteed on-demand, the floor is $0.98, set right now by Clore.ai. Step up to a managed neocloud and the same card lists at $3.20 on Hyperstack and n/a on Baseten, depending on how much tooling wraps it. Reserve it for a multi-year term and a published commitment rate drops to $2.24 (Paperspace's three-year price - Paperspace), while the hyperscalers' flexible on-demand rates run from $5.38 ( Google Cloud) to $10.00 per GPU at Oracle. That is one chip, the identical H100 silicon, carrying rates from $0.82 to $12.29 an hour at the same instant, entirely because of the promise attached to each. "The price of an H100" is not a number, it is a distribution, and the whole task of shopping is finding where in that distribution your workload is allowed to sit.

...

The honest answer, on the study's evidence, is no, and the reason is a whipsaw most buyers missed. Zoom out from our six weeks to the last three years and the H100 tells the whole story. It rented for $7 to $10 an hour in the 2023-2024 scarcity - SiliconData. Then it collapsed 64% through 2025, down to $2.85 to $3.50 on the neoclouds, as more than 300 new providers flooded the market with capacity - Introl. And then, against everyone's expectation of a continued slide, it rebounded about 40%, from a low of $1.70/hr in October 2025 to $2.35/hr by March 2026 on one-year contracts, as capacity tightened again - SemiAnalysis. Our flat summer plateau is not the market stalling out of nowhere. It is the market catching its breath after a crash and a rebound, settling into a new equilibrium.

...

The mechanism is simple: providers sell idle capacity cheaply because an idle GPU earns nothing, and they reserve the right to reclaim it when a paying on-demand customer wants it. The discounts are advertised as up to 90% off on-demand at AWS - AWS and up to 91% at Google Cloud - Google Cloud. The catch is a short reclaim notice: AWS gives a two-minute warning - AWS docs, and Azure just 30 seconds - Microsoft.

...

In our live data the spot discount is often the difference between two very different bills. As of November 14, 2026, the B200 on-demand floor is $4.89 against a spot rate of $1.74 ( -64%) for the same card. The H100 SXM is $1.73 on-demand against $0.82 on spot. The previous-generation H100 NVL is the exception, with spot above its on-demand floor ( $1.42 against $0.98). The catch is entirely about workload shape: a fault-tolerant batch job, a checkpointed training run, or an offline inference sweep can absorb interruptions and should almost always run on spot, while a production inference endpoint serving live users cannot and should not.

...

The consistent floor-setter in our data has been the marketplace model. In the study window, Vast.ai held the cheapest rate for a striking number of cards, including the A100 80GB at $0.54, the A100 40GB at $0.27, and the RTX 4090 at $0.14, because its third-party hosts set prices by supply and demand with almost no overhead - Vast.ai. As of November 14, 2026, the A100 80GB floor is held by Vast.ai at $0.52, the A100 40GB floor by Vast.ai at $0.31, and the RTX 4090 floor by Vast.ai at $0.14. RunPod listed the broadest catalog we saw in the study, 30 distinct GPUs spanning community and on-demand tiers, which made it the practical first stop for availability. Note how far the floor sits below the advertised neocloud rate for the same card: the cheapest guaranteed H100 in our data is $1.73 from Vast.ai right now, while the larger neoclouds publish $3.20 (Hyperstack) and $3.99 (Lambda) for their H100 SXM - Lambda. On the newest silicon the floor shifted to specialist neoclouds in the study, with DeepInfra holding the cheapest B200 and B300 on-demand rates; as of November 14, 2026, those floors belong to DeepInfra ( $4.89) and DeepInfra ( $5.89).

results.title: GPU Rental Prices: H100, H200, B200 Cost Per Hour by Provider | Mercatus Blog
highlights:
H100 rents for $3.84 an hour on average, H200 for $4.43, B200 for $6.39, with a 4x to 6x spread between the cheapest and most expensive provider on each. Current hourly rates by provider from the Mercatus GPU Index, what an 8-GPU node costs per month, and how the hourly rate sets the floor under token prices.

...

An NVIDIA H100 rents for $3.84 per GPU-hour on average across 27 cloud providers, an H200 for $4.43 across 20, and a B200 for $6.39 across 12, as tracked by the Mercatus GPU Index on September 13, 2026. Those averages hide the number that actually matters to a buyer: the same H100 lists at $1.79 an hour from one provider and $10.00 from another. On an 8-GPU node running around the clock, that is the difference between $10,500 and $58,400 a month for identical hardware.

...

## GPU rental prices at a glance

Volume-weighted average on-demand price per GPU-hour, with the low and high across tracked providers. Prices in USD as of September 13, 2026.

| GPU | VRAM | Average $/GPU-hr | Range | Providers | 30-day change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B300 | 288GB HBM3e | $8.89 | $7.50 to $24.22 | 7 | +5.3% |
| B200 | 192GB HBM3e | $6.39 | $3.74 to $16.14 | 12 | 0.0% |
| AMD MI300X | 192GB HBM3 | $4.98 | $2.39 to $6.94 | 6 | -0.1% |
| H200 | 141GB HBM3e | $4.43 | $2.25 to $11.71 | 20 | -0.8% |
| H100 | 80GB HBM3 | $3.84 | $1.79 to $12.52 | 27 | -0.4% |
| RTX PRO 6000 | 96GB GDDR7 | $2.07 | $0.99 to $5.64 | 11 | +1.4% |
| A100 80GB | 80GB HBM2e | $2.05 | $0.82 to $4.89 | 18 | +0.4% |
| L40S | 48GB GDDR6 | $1.41 | $0.58 to $4.24 | 16 | 0.0% |

...

The H100 is the reference price, and it has been rising. At $3.84 it sits 6.1 percent above where it was 90 days ago ($3.62), with the period low on June 27 and the high of $3.87 on August 15. A GPU that launched in 2022 got more expensive to rent over the summer of 2026, which is not what a depreciation schedule would predict. Demand for inference capacity, not the age of the silicon, is setting the rate. The H100 GPU cost page covers what that hardware costs to buy outright.

The H200 premium over H100 is 15 percent for 76 percent more memory. At $4.43 against $3.84, the H200 is the cheapest HBM per dollar in the data-center tier: about 32GB per dollar-hour versus 21GB on the H100. For memory-bound inference, which is most of it, the H200 is the better deal on paper, and its 7-day move of -2.4 percent suggests providers are pricing it to fill.

Blackwell carries a 66 percent premium over Hopper. B200 at $6.39 is 1.66x the H100 rate. Whether that is worth it depends entirely on throughput per dollar on your workload, which is the calculation in GPU ROI. The B300 at $8.89, up 5.3 percent in 30 days, is the only data-center GPU in the table moving meaningfully in either direction.

## H100 rental price by provider

Lowest listed on-demand price per GPU-hour at each provider, sorted cheapest first, with the configurations offered. Two of the 27 tracked providers (AWS and Azure) are in the index but not in the per-provider snapshot below.

The shape of this table is the story of the GPU cloud market. Nineteen providers sit between $1.47 and $3.50. Then there is a gap, and the hyperscalers sit at $9.80 and $10.00, 2.5x the volume-weighted average and 5x the specialist floor. Vast.ai’s $1.47 is a spot and community marketplace rate and sits below the index’s own $1.79 floor, which applies outlier filtering.

The gap is not a mistake. Hyperscaler pricing bundles enterprise support, compliance, and integration with the rest of the platform. A buyer who needs those things is paying for them. A buyer who only needs the GPU is paying for them anyway if they rent from a hyperscaler, and the market has responded by building a tier of specialist providers whose entire business is the $2 to $3.50 row. Why the same hardware carries such different prices is covered in more depth in Why token prices differ, since the same forces set both markets.

results.title: Thirty-Two H200s, Fourteen Months: What the Actuals Show | ComputeLabs Research
highlights:
## What happened to rental rates

Our underwriting assumed rental rates would decline approximately 20% per year. It was intended as the conservative case.

Rates rose instead. Silicon Data's “H200 Neo-Cloud Index”, a daily benchmark of on-demand rates across a panel of neocloud providers, moved from $2.70 per GPU-hour on May 4th 2026 to $3.09 by July 27th, an increase of 14.4%. Over the same window, the premium paid for an H200 over an H100 widened from an average of 5.8% in May to 12.1% in July.¹ The index carries only a few months of daily history, so it is a directional signal rather than a settled trend, but the direction is the opposite of what our model assumed.

We attribute this to workload composition. Long-context inference is constrained by high-bandwidth memory capacity more than training is, and the H200's 141GB is often enough to hold a model on a single GPU that would otherwise have to be split across several.² We have no direct visibility into the buyer mix, so this is our reading rather than an observation.

That said, a rate index is not a revenue forecast. A fleet earns rate multiplied by utilization, and the two move independently. Our own revenue per GPU peaked in May and eased through the summer even as published rates continued to climb. Anyone underwriting this asset from a price index alone is capturing only one of the two variables that matter.

results.title: Nebius augmente de 20 % ses tarifs de location de GPU à compter du 1er oct. ; l’action bondit de 4 % le 17 sept. | Gate News
highlights: Selon Shay Boloor, stratège en chef chez Futurum Equities, Nebius a annoncé le 17 septembre qu’il augmenterait d’environ 20 % ses tarifs de location de GPU pour l’IA à compter du 1er octobre, les tarifs de ses anciens modèles H100 augmentant d’environ 17 %. Cette annonce a fait grimper l’action Nebius de 4,12 %, à 217,99 dollars, au cours de la séance. Cette décision témoigne d’une demande soutenue pour les ressources de calcul dédiées à l’IA et indique que même les GPU d’ancienne génération, comme le H100 lancé il y a quatre ans, conservent une valeur locative élevée et un important pouvoir de fixation des prix sur le marché.

highlights:

- Pasokan chip AI belum mengimbangi permintaan, dengan sebagian besar chip diperkirakan telah dipesan hingga 2027; industri juga membutuhkan investasi besar pada pusat data, jaringan, listrik, dan infrastruktur pendukung.

results.title: On September 7 the cheapest published H100 price we could find was $3.85 per GPU-hour, $0.68 above the traded index. On September 14 it was still $3.85, now $1.10 above. The published … | Bobby Clay
highlights:
On September 7 the cheapest published H100 price we could find was $3.85 per GPU-hour, $0.68 above the traded index. On September 14 it was still $3.85, now $1.10 above. The published price did not move. The index fell.

That gap is the whole issue. Not one comparable public on-demand rate across the nine providers we track came in more than 1% off last week, and the four board floors have not moved since August 24. The Ornn Compute Price Index did all the moving, and unlike the week before it moved in both directions, down 13.2% on H100 SXM and up 6.5% on B200 over the seven days to September 14.

On H200 and B200 the relationship runs the other way. The index now sits above the published floor, which makes the listed rate the cheaper of the two references. Worth confirming before a renewal rather than writing off as stale.
Nine providers, every figure dated.
